content:
Facts: Heir purchased co-heirs' undivided shares in specific estate property by deed, then sued remaining co-heir for dissolution of joint ownership regarding that single asset without involving other estate assets or co-heirs who sold their shares.
Legal Framework: Articles 732, 757-768 Italian Civil Code (estate division; universality principle); settled case law on obligatory effect of hereditary share sales (Cass. 4428/2018, 9543/2002, SU 5068/2016).
Interpretive Issues: Whether sale of undivided hereditary share transfers immediate ownership or creates mere obligation; admissibility of partial estate division affecting single asset when initiated against one co-heir without consent of all co-owners; scope of universality principle in estate division.
Principles Applied: Sale of undivided share in estate asset has purely obligatory effect; effectiveness conditioned upon assignment through division. Until division, asset remains in undivided joint ownership; buyer cannot obtain exclusive ownership pre-division. Estate division universality principle requires comprehensive division of entire estate unless all co-heirs consent to partial division, either by agreement or by not opposing limited claim scope. Defendant's right to extend claim scope is facultative, not obligatory; cannot impose duty to broaden litigation. Partial division claim inadmissible when: (a) brought against single co-heir; (b) concerning individual estate asset; (c) predicated on obligatory-effect-only sale; (d) without unanimous co-heir consent. No "valid uncodified reasons" justify deviation from universality principle where preliminary sale lacks immediate transferability.
